import pandas as pd

# Load the metric data for candidate components
metric_data = pd.concat([
    pd.read_parquet('/telemetry/row/metric/metric_node.parquet'),
    pd.read_parquet('/telemetry/row/metric/metric_container.parquet'),
    pd.read_parquet('/telemetry/row/metric/metric_service.parquet'),
    pd.read_parquet('/telemetry/row/metric/metric_middleware.parquet'),
    pd.read_parquet('/telemetry/row/metric/metric_app.parquet')
])

# Convert 'timestamp' and 'startTime' from float to datetime if not already done
metric_data['timestamp'] = pd.to_datetime(metric_data['timestamp'], unit='ms', utc=True)

# Define the time range in UTC+8
start_time = pd.Timestamp('2020-05-26 03:00:00', tz='Asia/Singapore')
end_time = pd.Timestamp('2020-05-26 03:30:00', tz='Asia/Singapore')

# Filter the dataset for the specified time range
filtered_data = metric_data[(metric_data['timestamp'] >= start_time) & (metric_data['timestamp'] <= end_time)]

# Calculate the mean and standard deviation for anomaly detection
mean_value = filtered_data['value'].mean()
std_value = filtered_data['value'].std()

# Define a threshold for anomalies (e.g., 2 standard deviations from the mean)
threshold_upper = mean_value + 2 * std_value
threshold_lower = mean_value - 2 * std_value

# Identify anomalies
anomalies = filtered_data[(filtered_data['value'] > threshold_upper) | (filtered_data['value'] < threshold_lower)]

# Return the anomalies detected
anomalies.to_dict(orient='records')

    pd.read_parquet('/telemetry/row/metric/metric_service.parquet'),
    pd.read_parquet('/telemetry/row/metric/metric_middleware.parquet'),
    pd.read_parquet('/telemetry/row/metric/metric_app.parquet')
])

# Convert 'timestamp' from float to datetime if not already done
metric_data['timestamp'] = pd.to_datetime(metric_data['timestamp'], unit='ms', utc=True)

# Define the time range in UTC+8
start_time = pd.Timestamp('2020-05-26 03:00:00', tz='Asia/Singapore')
end_time = pd.Timestamp('2020-05-26 03:30:00', tz='Asia/Singapore')

# Filter the dataset for the specified time range
filtered_data = metric_data[(metric_data['timestamp'] >= start_time) & (metric_data['timestamp'] <= end_time)]

# Extract relevant metrics for Redis instances
used_memory = filtered_data[filtered_data['name'] == 'used_memory']
maxmemory = filtered_data[filtered_data['name'] == 'maxmemory']

# Merge the two dataframes on 'bomc_id' and 'timestamp'
merged_data = pd.merge_asof(used_memory.sort_values('timestamp'), 
                             maxmemory.sort_values('timestamp'), 
                             on='timestamp', 
                             by='bomc_id', 
                             suffixes=('_used', '_max')
                            )

# Identify instances where used_memory approached or exceeded maxmemory
anomalies = merged_data[merged_data['value_used'] >= merged_data['value_max']]

# Return the identified Redis instances
anomalies[['bomc_id', 'timestamp', 'value_used', 'value_max']].to_dict(orient='records')

controller.analysis: The presence of network traffic records provides an opportunity to analyze for anomalies, such as spikes or drops in traffic that could correlate with the system failure.
controller.instruction: Analyze the network traffic data for any significant spikes or drops during the time range May 26, 2020, from 03:00 to 03:30.

trajectory.instruction: Analyze the network traffic data for any significant spikes or drops during the time range May 26, 2020, from 03:00 to 03:30.
trajectory.code:
import pandas as pd

# Load the metric data for candidate components
metric_data = pd.concat([
    pd.read_parquet('/telemetry/row/metric/metric_node.parquet'),
    pd.read_parquet('/telemetry/row/metric/metric_container.parquet'),
    pd.read_parquet('/telemetry/row/metric/metric_service.parquet'),
    pd.read_parquet('/telemetry/row/metric/metric_middleware.parquet'),
    pd.read_parquet('/telemetry/row/metric/metric_app.parquet')
])

# Convert 'timestamp' from float to datetime if not already done
metric_data['timestamp'] = pd.to_datetime(metric_data['timestamp'], unit='ms', utc=True)

# Define the time range in UTC+8
start_time = pd.Timestamp('2020-05-26 03:00:00', tz='Asia/Singapore')
end_time = pd.Timestamp('2020-05-26 03:30:00', tz='Asia/Singapore')

# Filter the dataset for the specified time range
filtered_data = metric_data[(metric_data['timestamp'] >= start_time) & (metric_data['timestamp'] <= end_time)]

# Extract network traffic metrics
incoming_traffic = filtered_data[filtered_data['name'] == 'Incoming_network_traffic']
outgoing_traffic = filtered_data[filtered_data['name'] == 'Outgoing_network_traffic']

# Combine incoming and outgoing traffic for analysis
network_traffic = pd.concat([incoming_traffic, outgoing_traffic])

# Calculate the mean and standard deviation for anomaly detection
mean_traffic = network_traffic['value'].mean()
std_traffic = network_traffic['value'].std()

# Define thresholds for significant spikes or drops (e.g., 2 standard deviations from the mean)
threshold_upper = mean_traffic + 2 * std_traffic
threshold_lower = mean_traffic - 2 * std_traffic

# Identify significant spikes or drops in network traffic
significant_changes = network_traffic[(network_traffic['value'] > threshold_upper) | (network_traffic['value'] < threshold_lower)]

# Return the significant changes detected
significant_changes[['bomc_id', 'timestamp', 'name', 'value']].to_dict(orient='records')

import pandas as pd

# Load the metric data for candidate components
metric_data = pd.concat([
    pd.read_parquet('/telemetry/row/metric/metric_node.parquet'),
    pd.read_parquet('/telemetry/row/metric/metric_container.parquet'),
    pd.read_parquet('/telemetry/row/metric/metric_service.parquet'),
    pd.read_parquet('/telemetry/row/metric/metric_middleware.parquet'),
    pd.read_parquet('/telemetry/row/metric/metric_app.parquet')
])

# Convert 'timestamp' from float to datetime if not already done
metric_data['timestamp'] = pd.to_datetime(metric_data['timestamp'], unit='ms', utc=True)

# Define the time range in UTC+8
start_time = pd.Timestamp('2020-05-26 03:00:00', tz='Asia/Singapore')
end_time = pd.Timestamp('2020-05-26 03:30:00', tz='Asia/Singapore')

# Filter the dataset for the specified time range
filtered_data = metric_data[(metric_data['timestamp'] >= start_time) & (metric_data['timestamp'] <= end_time)]

# Extract network traffic metrics
incoming_traffic = filtered_data[filtered_data['name'] == 'Incoming_network_traffic']
outgoing_traffic = filtered_data[filtered_data['name'] == 'Outgoing_network_traffic']

# Calculate average incoming and outgoing traffic
avg_incoming = incoming_traffic['value'].mean()
avg_outgoing = outgoing_traffic['value'].mean()

# Calculate standard deviation for incoming and outgoing traffic
std_incoming = incoming_traffic['value'].std()
std_outgoing = outgoing_traffic['value'].std()

# Define thresholds for deviations (e.g., 2 standard deviations from the mean)
threshold_incoming_upper = avg_incoming + 2 * std_incoming
threshold_incoming_lower = avg_incoming - 2 * std_incoming
threshold_outgoing_upper = avg_outgoing + 2 * std_outgoing
threshold_outgoing_lower = avg_outgoing - 2 * std_outgoing

# Identify deviations in incoming traffic
incoming_deviations = incoming_traffic[(incoming_traffic['value'] > threshold_incoming_upper) | (incoming_traffic['value'] < threshold_incoming_lower)]

# Identify deviations in outgoing traffic
outgoing_deviations = outgoing_traffic[(outgoing_traffic['value'] > threshold_outgoing_upper) | (outgoing_traffic['value'] < threshold_outgoing_lower)]

# Return the average traffic and deviations detected
{
    'avg_incoming': avg_incoming,
    'avg_outgoing': avg_outgoing,
    'incoming_deviations': incoming_deviations[['bomc_id', 'timestamp', 'value']].to_dict(orient='records'),
    'outgoing_deviations': outgoing_deviations[['bomc_id', 'timestamp', 'value']].to_dict(orient='records')
}

outgoing_deviations = filtered_data[(filtered_data['name'] == 'Outgoing_network_traffic') & (filtered_data['bomc_id'] == 'ZJ-001-072')]

# Combine the deviations into a single DataFrame for analysis

}
